# SOOS Governed Remediation Protocol (GRP)
# llms-grp.txt — SOOS Project
# Source: draft-sato-soos-grp-00
# Canonical path: https://soosproject.ai/drafts/grp/llms.txt
# Updated: July 14, 2026

## Section 1 — What This Draft Does

The Governed Remediation Protocol (GRP) specifies the normative remediation action set available to a SOOS governance kernel when agent execution encounters a governed failure condition. GRP defines four action classes — FALLBACK, RETRY, ESCALATE, ROLLBACK — with explicit authority boundaries that determine when each may proceed autonomously and when it must escalate to a human principal through the Human Escalation Mechanism (HEM).

GRP is a coordination draft. It introduces no new cryptographic or identity primitives. It specifies the governed coordination of mechanisms already defined in the SOOS suite: the fallback boundary rule from RGP (DEC-RGP-08), the escalation protocol from HEM, the audit obligations from GAR, and the session state machine from AEP.

GRP closes the gap between prohibition detection and agent response. Without GRP, every SOOS deployment builds ad hoc remediation logic — ungoverned, unauditable, and bypassing principal sovereignty.

## Section 2 — Key Normative Terms

GRP Action Class: One of four normative categories of governed remediation behavior: FALLBACK, RETRY, ESCALATE, ROLLBACK.

GRP Trigger Type: A categorized failure condition initiating GRP processing. Five types: GRP-T1 (PROHIBITION_BLOCK — Cedar DENY), GRP-T2 (RESOURCE_FAILURE — RGP unavailability), GRP-T3 (EXECUTION_FAILURE — AEP STALLED/ERROR), GRP-T4 (MANDATE_BOUNDARY — MAD scope violation), GRP-T5 (CONSENT_ABSENT — Cedar consent failure).

Change Event: A structured, signed, machine-readable message from a registered publisher indicating a dependency, resource, or mandate condition relevant to an active agent session has changed.

External Publisher Registry (EPR): A kernel-managed Sovereign Object containing registration records for P-TYPE-2 (non-SOOS) change event publishers. Includes signing key, validity window, permitted event types.

DEC-RGP-08: The three-condition autonomous fallback test, adopted verbatim from draft-sato-soos-rgp-00 §13.1. Three conditions must ALL pass for autonomous FALLBACK without HEM: (1) fallback trust_level ≥ primary trust_level; (2) fallback capability_class covers the sub-goal; (3) fallback cost_model + prior commitments ≤ MJWT Resource Envelope budget. Authoritative source: RGP §13.1.

Remediation Tier: Cedar-classified authority level for a GRP action: autonomous / notify / approve / escalate.

RETRY ceiling: Maximum autonomous retry attempts from MJWT mandate retry_policy. Default if absent: 3.

rollback_nonce: Session-scoped nonce generated by GEC at ROLLBACK initiation. Prevents replay. Session-bound.

propagation_scope: SACR field declaring which cluster identifiers the GEC may propagate change signals to. Cross-cluster propagation is pre-authorized; it is not negotiated at event time.

P-TYPE-1 Publisher: SOOS IDP principal with active KIA credential. Highest trust. KIA signature verification.

P-TYPE-2 Publisher: Non-SOOS entity registered in EPR with asymmetric signing key. Trust-on-first-registration.

P-TYPE-3 Publisher: Publisher exposing /.well-known/soos-grp-publisher (analogous to OIDC discovery). Discovery-based trust via pre-configured TLS trust anchor. Appropriate for GitHub Security Advisories, npm, PyPI, CSAF feeds.

## Section 3 — Architecture and Relationships

GRP position in the SOOS stack:

```
CAP (Cedar DENY) → GRP-T1
AEP (STALLED/ERROR) → GRP-T3
RGP (resource failure, ALE-025) → GRP-T2
MAD (mandate boundary) → GRP-T4
CAP (consent absent) → GRP-T5
        ↓
GRP: publisher verify → impact assessment → Cedar tier → action class → DEC-RGP-08 (FALLBACK) → execute or HEM
        ↓ autonomous               ↓ HEM required
  ALE-065..069                ALE-067 + HEM class → human decision → resume
```

GRP sits above RGP and AEP (receives their failure signals) and below HEM (routes escalation requests to it). GRP has no downstream dependents in the current SOOS suite — it is the terminal protocol for session failure response.

Trigger-to-action-class mapping:
- GRP-T1: FALLBACK, ESCALATE (RETRY not eligible — Cedar would DENY again)
- GRP-T2: FALLBACK, RETRY, ESCALATE
- GRP-T3: RETRY, ROLLBACK, ESCALATE
- GRP-T4: ESCALATE only
- GRP-T5: ESCALATE only

HEM class map (key entries):
- DEC-RGP-08 Condition 1 fail (trust decrease) → HEM-HIGH-1
- DEC-RGP-08 Condition 2 fail (capability mismatch) → HEM-PRE-2
- DEC-RGP-08 Condition 3 fail (budget exceeded) → HEM-DS-1
- RETRY ceiling reached → HEM-PRE-2
- GRP-T4 (mandate boundary) → HEM-HIGH-1
- GRP-T5 (consent absent) → HEM-CONSENT
- Post-ROLLBACK → HEM-HIGH-1
- Multiple failures: highest-priority class wins (HEM-HIGH-1 > HEM-CONSENT > HEM-PRE-2 > HEM-DS-1)

FALLBACK pre-declaration requirement: The fallback candidate MUST be pre-declared in the IDP EOD before session start. The GEC MUST NOT autonomously activate an undeclared fallback.

RETRY: Exponential backoff, minimum 1 second interval, ceiling from MJWT retry_policy (default 3). Every attempt: ALE-065.

ROLLBACK: rollback_nonce session-scoped; must reference target ALE seq number; WAL verification required; ALE-068 before execution, ALE-069 on completion + HEM-HIGH-1 for human review.

Cross-cluster: Pre-authorized in SACR propagation_scope. Each receiving GEC independently verifies SACR + KIA signature + performs own impact assessment. Failure → ALE-064 rejection_reason: "cross_cluster_authority_failure".

## Section 4 — GAR ALE Types (new in this draft)

GRP defines ALE-064 through ALE-069 as new GAR Audit Log Entry types:

ALE-064: GRP_EVENT_REJECTED
  Triggers: publisher verification failure, session nonce mismatch, no impact match,
  DEC-RGP-08 condition failure, cross-cluster authority failure.
  Key fields: event_id, publisher_id, rejection_reason, session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

ALE-065: GRP_RETRY_ATTEMPTED
  Trigger: RETRY action class execution.
  Key fields: event_id, resource_id, attempt_count, elapsed_ms,
  mandate_budget_remaining, session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

ALE-066: GRP_FALLBACK_ACTIVATED
  Trigger: FALLBACK action class execution (autonomous or HEM-authorized).
  Key fields: event_id, primary_resource_id, fallback_resource_id, autonomous (bool),
  dec_rgp08_cond1_pass (bool), dec_rgp08_cond2_pass (bool), dec_rgp08_cond3_pass (bool),
  hem_decision_ref (if autonomous: false), session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

ALE-067: GRP_ESCALATE_TRIGGERED
  Trigger: ESCALATE action class; HEM entry.
  Key fields: event_id, hem_class, trigger_type,
  action_classes_attempted (array), session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

ALE-068: GRP_ROLLBACK_INITIATED
  Trigger: ROLLBACK action class initiation.
  Key fields: event_id, target_ale_ref, rollback_nonce,
  session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

ALE-069: GRP_ROLLBACK_COMPLETED
  Trigger: ROLLBACK action class completion.
  Key fields: event_id, target_ale_ref, rollback_nonce,
  rollback_status (SUCCESS/PARTIAL/FAILED), session_id, timestamp, prev_span_hash.

Chain traceability: ALE-069 and the final resolution ALE MUST carry a reference to the initiating trigger ALE (e.g., RGP ALE-025 or CAP CEDAR_DENY ALE). Enables single-query trigger → attempts → outcome reconstruction.

## Section 5 — Dependency Graph

GRP depends on (normative):
- draft-sato-soos-rgp-00: DEC-RGP-08 (verbatim adoption, §13.1), Resource Map SO, ALE-025 trigger
- draft-sato-soos-aep-02: session states (STALLED/ERROR), EOD fallback pre-declaration
- draft-sato-soos-hem-05: all ESCALATE routing (HEM-HIGH-1, HEM-PRE-2, HEM-DS-1, HEM-LIM-1, HEM-CONSENT)
- draft-sato-soos-cap-04: Cedar DENY trigger (GRP-T1), SUSPENDED state → ROLLBACK, consent failure (GRP-T5)
- draft-sato-soos-gar-03: ALE-064 through ALE-069 consumer
- draft-sato-soos-mad-03: SACR propagation_scope, mandate scope validation (GRP-T4)
- draft-sato-soos-idp-05: EOD fallback pre-declaration, P-TYPE-1 publisher registration
- draft-sato-soos-kia-03: P-TYPE-1 signature verification, GEC integrity (P5, P2 via KEE-1)
- draft-sato-soos-sov-02: EPR as kernel-managed SO instance
- draft-sato-soos-mjwt-02: retry_policy, remediation_policy, Resource Envelope
- draft-sato-soos-kee-00: GEC integrity (KEE-1 P5 hash-lock, P2 FROST threshold signing)
- RFC 2119, RFC 8174, RFC 8446, RFC 7517

GRP is consumed by: (no current SOOS drafts depend on GRP downstream)

## Section 6 — Implementation and Deployment Status

Status: draft-sato-soos-grp-00, submitted to IETF Datatracker, July 2026.

Reference implementation: Ponyhouse Farm (ponyhouse.myauberge.jp) serves as the reference supplier for the CAP-EXP FALLBACK use case in Appendix A. The ATP booking agent at MyAuberge K.K. is the GRP reference deployment for the FALLBACK and RETRY action classes.

Open questions deferred post-Vienna:
- OQ-GRP-02: Change Applicability Statement (CAS) complete schema, publication target, REQUIRED vs RECOMMENDED
- OQ-GRP-03: Cross-cluster multi-hop propagation query interface (A→B→C)
- OQ-GRP-06: Change event format as standalone IETF draft vs. GRP-internal schema

Vienna engagement: GRP is part of the SOOS suite presented at IETF 126 Vienna (July 18-24, 2026). Relevant WGs: WIMSE (workload identity), SCITT (supply chain integrity), OAuth (mandate token model).

Japan government track: GRP's publisher identity model (P-TYPE-3 for upstream advisory feeds) and HEM-enforced human oversight boundary are architecturally consistent with emerging AI governance requirements for human oversight of autonomous AI systems across multiple jurisdictions. The disaster response use case (§1.2) is directly applicable to governance-layer requirements for the Japan emergency response AI deployment track.

Developer value proposition: "Your agents can fix their own dependencies, governed by your policies, with human approval where it matters."
